subject: Stan for MC sampling of Ising states

messages.author: 761b6cba0a118b93
messages.subject: Stan for MC sampling of Ising states
parts:
Hi,

Can one use Stan for MC sampling of Ising states? Basically here you start with some initial configuration of lattice, flip spins randomly, have some acceptance criteria based on some thermodynamic variable you compute, then accept or reject the next state and you do this progressively. So each state is discrete and so are other parameters and I am not sure how to pipe in Stan into my simulation i.e. what the ‘model’ is, or what the priors are. I thought for large lattice sizes using optimized libraries such as yours would make the simulations faster, hence the interest.

Best,

Jeyashree

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Stan for MC sampling of Ising states
parts:
Nope.  There are various tricks for trying to embed Ising-like models into
continuous spaces where something like Stan could be used, but those
embeddings introduce their own pathologies which obstruct efficient
computation.  Ultimately this is all due to the fact that we don’t know how
to efficiently move through even structured discrete spaces.

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Stan for MC sampling of Ising states
parts:
No, we currently do not know how to efficiently sample from
discrete spaces which is the reason we do not support discrete
parameters in Stan.  There are cases where you can marginalize
out discrete parameters (for example discrete latent classifications)
to gives a well-posed continuous model, but Ising models are not
one of them.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Stan for MC sampling of Ising states
parts:
There's a cottage entire industry devoted to fitting Ising models.
That's precisely because nobody knows how to fit them reliably.
They're NP-complete, in general, so there's good reason to believe
they're fundamentally intractable (no polynomial algorithm in the number
of states exists to solve them):

https://www.siam.org/pdf/news/654.pdf

You probably don't want to reinvent the wheel here, but I don't
know which packages to recommend for special cases that might be
tractable or that provide heuristic approximations to the intractable
general case.

Just pulling out a naive discrete sampler (either Metropolis or Gibbs)
isn't going to work due to the stability of local optima and the combinatorial
number of states requiring exploration, no matter how much parallel computing
power you throw at it.

- Bob
